headline: The last isolated showers over San Diego County end by mid-morning Friday, leading into a cool, dry weekend, a slight chance of very light showers Sunday night into Monday, and warming to above-normal temperatures for Thanksgiving and Friday.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Isolated light showers over San Diego County, including the coast, should end by mid-morning Friday as the storm system departs and drier air moves in; patchy fog in the Inland Empire can cut visibility below 2 miles until about 9 AM. The rest of Friday will be cool and dry, with highs in the 60s along the coast and in the valleys, 40s in the mountains, mid 50s in the high desert, and low 70s in the low desert. West winds gusting around 30–35 mph blow through mountain passes into the deserts until about 3 PM, and skies are mostly clear Friday night.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A very weak breeze from the land (offshore) Saturday morning makes Saturday slightly warmer and drier, and Sunday stays about the same as the ocean breeze returns, with fair weather and occasional high clouds. Another weak storm system passes quickly Sunday night into Monday morning, bringing a slight chance of light showers from the mountains west to the coast; about a quarter of computer model runs keep it completely dry, and any rain would likely be just a few hundredths of an inch. Snow levels would be near 6,500 feet, but with so little moisture only a few flurries are expected.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: High pressure brings drier, warmer weather late Monday and Tuesday, with another round of weak offshore breezes Tuesday morning. Wednesday is uncertain: one model shows a deep storm bringing much colder, wetter weather, but it is an outlier, and most forecasts aim the moisture at Northern California, so the official chance of rain Wednesday is only 15–20%. After that, high pressure builds in, with weak offshore breezes possible as early as Thanksgiving morning and strengthening Friday; Thanksgiving highs are forecast 2 to 7 degrees above normal, warming to about 5 to 10 degrees above normal on Friday.

coast: Elevated surf continues at 3–5 feet with sets to 7 feet, highest on west-facing beaches, with strong rip currents and minor coastal flooding during high tides (Beach Hazards Statement for the Orange and San Diego County coasts until 9 AM Friday). King Tides peak next week: tides above 7 feet are possible as early as Saturday, Nov. 21, and morning high tides may top 8 feet next Tuesday through Thursday, bringing widespread moderate impacts. For boaters, winds and seas ease Friday morning but pick up again Friday afternoon and evening, especially well offshore; a Small Craft Advisory runs until 9 PM Friday for waters 10 to 60 nautical miles out from San Mateo Point to the Mexican border, including San Clemente Island. No further marine hazards are expected through Tuesday.
watch_for: King Tides: above 7 feet possible from Saturday and above 8 feet on morning high tides next Tuesday–Thursday, with widespread moderate impacts.
Slight chance of light showers Sunday night into Monday morning, mountains to the coast (only a few hundredths of an inch if any).
Wednesday's system: most likely just a 15–20% rain chance, but one outlier model shows a much colder, wetter storm.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the cool, dry weekend and the warm-up toward Thanksgiving, less sure whether Sunday night–Monday brings any measurable rain, and have low confidence in the track and strength of Wednesday's system.
